name: George Washington
hook: Father of his Country: the cherry tree, Valley Forge and the first presidency in seven facts.

facts.label: the first president
facts.statement: He was sworn in on April 30, 1789 at Federal Hall in New York City and is the only president who never lived in Washington, D.C.

facts.label: Mount Vernon
facts.statement: Mount Vernon was his Virginia estate on the Potomac; he retired there in 1797 and died two years later.

facts.label: surveyor
facts.statement: He got his surveyor's license from the College of William & Mary in 1749.

facts.label: Fort Necessity
facts.statement: He led the building of Fort Necessity in 1754 and surrendered there during the French and Indian War.

facts.label: Valley Forge
facts.statement: His army wintered at Valley Forge in 1777-78, and the Marquis de Lafayette was with him there.

facts.label: the cherry tree
facts.statement: The cherry tree story comes from Parson Weems's 1806 biography of him, not from Washington himself.

facts.label: Gilbert Stuart
facts.statement: Gilbert Stuart painted the portrait of him that is used on the one-dollar bill; one version left his head unfinished.
